result.title: Dynamics Forcing: Mitigating Error Accumulation in Causal Video World Models
result.summary: Causal video world models generate block by block from their own previous outputs. Small errors in early blocks are fed back as history and grow until the scene and the robot fall apart. Teacher forcing trains on clean ground-truth history, so the model never sees the history it will actually condition on, and it also finds a shortcut: copying the previous frame instead of predicting how the scene changes. We present Dynamics Forcing, a training scheme that keeps real video as the only supervision and reshapes how history is presented. History is perturbed in three ways: random noising, self-resampling by the model itself, and joint denoising, in which the most recent blocks are still partly noisy when the next block is predicted. On top of this we move history guidance and first-frame anchor guidance from inference into training, so that the model is pushed to use its history and its reference frame rather than ignore them. Dynamics Forcing needs no teacher model, no distillation, and no additional model at inference. Applied to a 5B video model with LoRA on 77 hours of manipulation video on a single GPU, it better matches unseen real continuations and reduces error accumulation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Dynamics Forcing 训练方案：在因果视频世界模型中用随机加噪、模型自重采样和「最近块仍带噪」的联合去噪来改写历史呈现方式，并把历史引导与首帧锚定引导从推理移入训练，以缓解误差累积和复制前一帧的捷径，无需教师模型、蒸馏或额外推理模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把模型自生成、部分带噪的中间历史作为训练条件并提供引导监督，可能为 LVR 中基于自生成轨迹的训练、干净前缀监督带来的 exposure bias，以及中间 latent 状态的使用与贡献分配提供可核查的方法线索；但研究对象是视频世界模型，与 VLM 推理状态的联系需人工判断。
